newsitem.title: JAPAN: LME firm in Asia, copper seen heading for $2,550.
newsitem.headline: LME firm in Asia, copper seen heading for $2,550.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) copper and aluminium prices were firm in quiet Asian trade on Wednesday and copper was expected to head for the next target of $2,550, traders said.
"Sentiment is strong. Market participants expect copper to head towards $2,550," said a trader at a Japanese trading house.
"This might also pull up aluminium, sentiment for which is weak after breaching its support at $1,650 yesterday."
At 0455 GMT, LME benchmark three-month copper was quoted at $2,502/07 a tonne, up from $2,500 at 1800 GMT on Tuesday and $2,393 at the afternoon kerb close on Tuesday.
Traders said a decision by U.S. authorities to leave interest rates unchanged was also positive for the metal market as it would help maintain brisk U.S. economic growth.
But some were worried about possible profit-taking after a rise on Tuesday took copper to levels last seen a year ago, before the Sumitomo Corp scandal.
"I wouldn't be surprised if we saw profit-taking," said one trader. "I don't believe the market can sustain this level."
Traders did not pay much attention to Tuesday's report of a rise in aluminium stocks of 2,050 tonnes in London, the first increase since early April.
But they were concerned that the metal broke its support level at $1,650, escaping from the $1,650-$1,680 range of the past 10 days.
"In the near future, we expect inventories to continue declining. But the metal might ease," one trader said.
